explanation: Smart pointers in C++ are template classes that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They are used to implement RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idioms, providing safer and more expressive memory management compared to raw pointers. Modern C++ emphasizes the use of smart pointers to handle ownership semantics explicitly, with std::unique_ptr for exclusive ownership and std::shared_ptr for shared ownership scenarios.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of modern C++ smart pointers: std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr. The unique_ptr manages a Resource object with exclusive ownership, automatically deleting it when it goes out of scope, exemplifying RAII. The shared_ptr manages shared ownership of a Resource, with reference counting ensuring the resource is destroyed only when the last shared_ptr is destroyed. This showcases how smart pointers facilitate safe, automatic memory management aligned with modern C++ best practices.
